items.text: Where can I see what's happening with my transfer?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

You can check your transfer status by logging into your Wise account, going to Home to see your activity list, and clicking on the specific transfer you want to track. Once logged in, you'll see statuses like "Your money's being processed," "Money received," or "Transfer Sent." Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: What do the different stages in the tracker mean?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

The tracker shows three main stages: "Your money's being processed" means we are waiting for your bank to send funds. "Money received" means we have your cash and are converting it. Finally, "Transfer Sent" means we have sent the money to your recipient's bank, but their bank still needs time to process and deliver it.

Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: My payment has said processing since Tuesday, is that normal?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

If your transfer has been "processing" for more than two working days, you should check with your bank to ensure they have sent the money to us. Sometimes banks take longer to process transfers on weekends or public holidays. You can also ask your recipient to provide a transfer receipt to help track the payment. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: What does transfer sent mean?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

"Transfer Sent" means we've sent the money to your recipient's bank, but their bank still needs time to process and deliver it. This can take a few working days depending on where you're sending the money. Your money is safely on its way, but the tracker might not update again until it arrives in their account. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: How long until the money shows up for my recipient?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

The estimated arrival time is based on your transfer's current stage and the recipient's bank processing times. If it says "Transfer Sent," the recipient's bank usually needs one to four working days to release the funds. Weekends and public holidays are excluded from these estimates.

Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: It was supposed to arrive today and nothing's there.

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

We mark transfers as complete once we've sent the money to your recipient's bank, but their bank may take up to one working day to process it. If you have a transfer receipt, ask your recipient to check their bank statement for Wise or look for the reference number provided in our email.

items.text: Do bank holidays slow transfers down?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Yes, bank holidays can slow transfers down because banks don't process payments on weekends or public holidays. Our delivery estimates only count working days from Monday to Friday. If you send money before a holiday, it might not move until the next working day.

items.text: Will a small typo in the name stop the payment?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Small typos in names usually don't stop payments for most countries. However, for some currencies like Japanese Yen, even a small spelling error can cause issues. If your recipient's bank details are wrong, the money might take longer to arrive or get sent back to us.

items.text: The person I paid says they haven't received a thing.

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

We mark your transfer as complete once we've sent the money to their bank, but their bank may still be processing it. They can ask their bank to speed this up by sharing a transfer receipt with all the details.

Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: How do I get a receipt to send to my recipient's bank?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

To get a receipt, log into your Wise account, click on your transfer, and use the three dots menu to download the PDF. You can then save it to your device and send it directly to your recipient so their bank has all the details needed to track the money. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: Why is it marked completed if my brother still can't see the money?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

We mark your transfer as complete once we've sent the money to your brother's bank. His bank might still be processing it, which can take up to one working day. He should check his bank statement for a transaction from Wise or our partner, looking at the reference number rather than your name. If he sees the funds but in a different currency, his bank may have converted them again. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: What name will show on my recipient's bank statement?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

The sender name on your recipient's bank statement might not be your own name; instead, it could appear as Wise or one of our banking partners. You can use the transfer receipt to help them identify the transaction by checking the reference number and amount. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: The amount that arrived is different from what I sent.

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER
If the amount differs, your recipient's bank may have converted the currency again, resulting in a different total. You can use the transfer receipt to check the sender name and reference number on their statement. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: Why is this taking so long?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Delays often happen because your bank is still sending the money to us, security checks are running, or the recipient's bank needs time to process it. Weekends and public holidays also slow things down since banks don't work then. If it has been more than two days for your money to reach us, you should check with your own bank to confirm they've sent it.

items.text: How long does a bank transfer take to reach Wise?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Bank transfers usually take one to four working days to reach us. If your money is still being processed for more than two days, check with your bank to ensure they've sent it. Weekends and public holidays also delay processing. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: Is paying by card faster than a bank transfer?
Why would you need to verify my information?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

We may need extra information to meet regulations. If we do, we'll send you an email explaining what we need. Keep an eye on your inbox so you can provide it quickly. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: My transfer is coming back to me, why?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

If your transfer is returning to you, it's likely because there was an error in the recipient's details, such as a typo in their name or account number. Their bank may have rejected the payment and sent it back. You can check your activity list to confirm this status.

items.text: What counts as a proof of payment?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

A proof of payment is a document showing you've sent money from your bank account. It must clearly show your details, your bank's name, our details, the date, amount, currency, and reference number. We can't accept text copied into an email or photos of computer screens. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: Can I upload two screenshots as proof?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Yes, you can send us up to five files total, including two screenshots. Both must clearly show your bank account number so we know they are from the same account. We cannot accept text copied and pasted or photos of computer screens. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: What file size can my bank statement be?
What does a pacs.008 document mean for Swift payments?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

For Swift payments, the proof of payment we need is an pacs.008 document. This is a specific file type required to verify your bank transfer. If you can't provide it, your verification might be delayed. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: Where does my recipient use the reference number?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Your recipient uses the banking partner reference number to check where their transfer is once it shows as complete on your Wise account. They should give this number to their bank if they need help tracking the payment, as banks may call it a UTR or transaction reference number depending on the country. Anything else about your transfer?

items.text: What's the difference between the transfer number and the partner reference?

llm.label: in
llm.reply:
ANSWER

Your transfer number is for contacting Wise directly if you need help with your transfer. The banking partner reference number is given to your recipient so they can track where the money is once it shows as complete on your account. In some countries, like India, this partner number might be called a UTR or transaction reference.
